releases.title: July 2026
releases.summary: A batch of new features, fixes, and under-the-hood hardening — all landed on main, all covered by tests, all running on your machine.

entries.headline: Adjustable AI cleanup, from a light touch to a full polish
entries.body: Pick how much the AI reshapes your words — None, Low, Medium, or High — and OpenWhisp always keeps your raw transcript so you can revert to exactly what you said in one click.

entries.headline: Voice editing — "scratch that", "delete last sentence", "undo"
entries.body: Fix a misspoken phrase without deleting and re-dictating. A deterministic, offline command layer edits the in-progress text before it's committed. No AI required.

entries.headline: A self-learning dictionary that tunes itself
entries.body: When you type over a transcription to correct it, OpenWhisp notices the fix and proposes it as a vocabulary term — learning your jargon on your machine, never on someone's server.

entries.headline: Richer local formatting — numbers, lists, and markdown
entries.body: Opt-in rules turn spoken structure into clean text: "bullet…" into a list, "twenty twenty-six" into 2026, "bold that" into markdown — all deterministic, all off by default so nothing surprises you.

entries.headline: Send dictations beyond the focused app
entries.body: Foundational plumbing for routing a transcript somewhere other than the app you're in — a file, a Shortcut, a webhook. Built to fail open: if a target can't take it, your text still lands where it always did. Never dropped.

entries.headline: Silence no longer errors on one backend but not the other
entries.body: Dictating nothing now quietly produces nothing on both whisper backends — no more stray error toast depending on which engine you'd picked in Advanced settings.

entries.headline: OpenWhisp can't accidentally kill your other whisper servers
entries.body: The engine now checks a process is one it actually launched — by full path, not just name — before signaling it, so your own Homebrew or hand-built whisper-server is safe. Plus a fix for a startup port race.

entries.headline: A data race in Apple Speech dictation, closed
entries.body: Session state is now confined to a single context, so a late recognition callback can never leak a partial from one dictation into the next.

entries.headline: Agent rate limiting counts sessions on one honest clock
entries.body: The per-client session cap could be bypassed by a long-running session straddling the window edge. It now measures membership and expiry on the same clock, so the cap holds.

entries.headline: Post-processing scripts clean up after themselves
entries.body: Timed-out post-processing scripts now reap reliably — honest about best-effort process-group isolation, with a guarded kill that can never signal OpenWhisp's own processes.

entries.headline: The audio-device watcher tears down cleanly
entries.body: The CoreAudio listener that notices when you plug in a mic now removes itself symmetrically — no lingering, unremovable observer.

entries.headline: One place for text transforms
entries.body: The dictation pipeline now runs through a single, ordered post-processing chain — the groundwork that lets new transforms and output targets drop in cleanly, with behavior verified byte-for-byte against the old path.

entries.headline: Corrupt settings files can't take the app down
entries.body: All five on-device data stores now share one hardened loader: a bad file is quarantined and the app carries on with sane defaults, instead of a fix living in only one of them.

entries.headline: End-to-end audio testing, so features stay working
entries.body: A full regression suite now feeds pre-recorded audio through the whole pipeline — the reason "757 tests passing" is more than a number. Every feature above ships with coverage.
